episodes.160938: Thunderstorms produced isolated gusty winds during the afternoon, with additional gusty winds in the evening and overnight.
episodes.160958: A line of thunderstorms produced sporadic wind damage across north-central Maryland.
episodes.160993: Thunderstorms brought locally heavy rain to the Lehigh Valley of Pennsylvania on the night of September 8.  Rainfall totals were as high as 2 to 5 inches.
episodes.160994: Thunderstorms brought locally heavy rain to Warren County in New Jersey on the night of September 8.  Rainfall totals were as high as 2 to 5 inches.
episodes.161026: Showers and storms developed along a southward moving outflow boundary and low-level trough. Enough instability and enhanced winds aloft allowed some storms to become strong as they approached and moved offshore of the coasts of Brevard, Indian River, St. Lucie, and Martin counties.
episodes.161027: A high coverage of showers and thunderstorms occurred across east central Florida due to a late-day sea breeze collision. West to southwest steering winds allowed some of these thunderstorms to  move toward and offshore of the Volusia and Brevard county coasts in the early evening hours.
episodes.161181: A broken line of showers and isolated thunderstorms developed over central Pennsylvania during the afternoon of September 9, 2021, ahead of a secondary cold front crossing the region. One of these storms produced wind damage in western Franklin County.
episodes.161506: The large upper high pressure center over the Great Basin not only provided much of the area with near record heat, but also spread some tropical moisture into the area on September 9 which resulted in scattered thunderstorms during the afternoon.  Moderate to heavy rainfall occured with some of the thunderstorms in the Kern County Deserts and along the Kern River Valley where several stations measured over half an inch of rainfall.  Between a quarter and a half inch of rainfell in portions of the south end of the Upper Sierra.  The rainfall was less significant elsewhere with most stations picking up betweeen a trace to a tenth of an inch of rainfall.  A few of the thunderstorms also produced strong outflow wind gusts in the Kern County Deserts.
episodes.161578: Tropical Storm Mindy pushed through North Florida in the morning hours dragging a weak trough behind it. That coupled with a moist southwesterly flow produced many marine wind gust.
episodes.161836: Isolated dry thunderstorms across central Nevada caused gusty outflow winds.
episodes.162055: Tropical Storm Mindy developed just southwest of the area and moved northeastward, bringing with it heavy rain and gusty winds with several reports of trees and power lines down and some flooding.  Two homes were damaged in Leon county from falling trees, but no injuries were reported.  One brief tornado occurred in a rural, forested area of Wakulla county with no structural damage.
episodes.162288: A cold front moved into the mid-Atlantic late on September 8. Widespread showers and thunderstorms developed in a warm and humid air mass ahead of the front, moving into eastern Pennsylvania during the evening and early overnight hours. With instability waning after dark, much of the convection remained sub-severe. However, some instances of damaging wind did occur, particularly along a bowing line segment in Berks County. Showers and storms continued to gradually weaken as they shifted east later in the night.
episodes.162431: A slow moving frontal boundary along with an approaching upper level disturbance triggered a strong thunderstorm across the coastal waters.
episodes.162432: A slow moving frontal boundary along with an approaching upper level disturbance triggered severe thunderstorms across Southern Connecticut.
episodes.162554: The combination of near normal moisture, southeasterly flow, and strong daytime heating and local effects aided in the generation of strong shower and thunderstorm activity across portions of north-central and northwestern Puerto Rico during the afternoon hours.
episodes.162869: Scattered thunderstorms produced heavy rain and severe wind gusts across the Inland Empire, mountains and deserts on Thursday, September 9, leading to flooding, debris flows and rock slides. Elevated convection also made it to the coast on September 9. On September 10, severe thunderstorms producing heavy rainfall impacted the lower deserts.
episodes.163003: Weak high pressure over the western Atlantic promoted weak southwesterly low-level flow across the area along with sufficient moisture. The weak flow pushed the Gulf Sea Breeze inland and towards the east coast while the Atlantic Sea Breeze pinned along the east coast, with outflow boundaries in all directions. Multiple waterspouts formed from showers and storms over the Atlantic waters.
episodes.163041: A cluster of showers and storms producing heavy rain develop across Warren County in central North Carolina along a slow moving mid level disturbance in advance of a slow moving cold front. The heavy rain produced a couple of reports fo flash flooding across Warren County.
episodes.163044: A band of slow moving showers and thunderstorms producing heavy rain along a slow moving cold front and produced flash flooding across Wake County in central North Carolina.
episodes.163095: A slow moving cold front, instability ahead of it, and low level wind shear led to a brief, isolated weak tornado in the overnight hours in Coventry, Connecticut.
episodes.163096: A slow moving cold front, instability, and a low level jet combined to produce an isolated tornado in northern Connecticut during the early morning hours and then a waterspout over Cape Cod Bay near Wellfleet during the mid-afternoon.
episodes.163200: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms resulted in widespread damage over eastern New York on Wednesday September 8, 2021.
episodes.163218: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms resulted in damage over southern Vermont on Wednesday September 8, 2021.
episodes.163221: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms resulted in damage over western Massachusetts on Wednesday September 8, 2021.
episodes.163275: Showers and thunderstorms produced locally heavy rainfall that led to isolated instances of flooding and flash flooding.
episodes.163276: Showers and thunderstorms produced locally heavy rainfall that led isolated instances of flooding.
episodes.163436: Scattered thunderstorms along a frontal boundary produced heavy rain which caused flash flooding across portions of southeast Virginia.
episodes.163457: Cold advection from another cold frontal passage allowed for sufficient instability to develop over Lake Erie for some early morning waterspouts. Shear increased as the day ensued, minimizing the threat.
episodes.164149: A weak tornado (or landspout) developed near the community of Lake Los Angeles. No damage was reported.

In Coventry, a short-lived tornado touched down near the intersection of South Street and Pucker Street, downing several large trees in a field.  It had a discontinuous path as it traveled to the east-northeast across a wooded area, where it created pockets of tree damage.  It then touched down again just north of the intersection of Flanders Road and Nathan Hale Drive, where it damaged power lines and then moved through another wooded area.  At least 50 trees were damaged in this area, with many having their tops sheared off.  More than a dozen trees were blown down.  It appears that the tornado dissipated quickly after that, since no other significant damage was observed farther to the northeast.  No homes in the area had any damage.  Two residents reported hearing the tornado warning, moving to safety in their basement, and then about 15 minutes later hearing a loud wind that lasted just moments.  The tornado is estimated to have been on the ground no more than 90 seconds.
